brief: A 3D-printed PLA flight-controller mounting plate for a drone, 80 mm long, 60 mm wide and 4 mm thick, with all four corners rounded to an 8 mm radius. Four 3.2 mm holes on a 30.5 mm square of centres, centred on the plate, for the flight-controller stack. Four 3.4 mm frame holes on a 64 x 44 mm rectangle of centres, centred on the plate. A 16 mm cable hole in the centre of the plate. Two 16 x 4 mm zip-tie slots running along the plate's length, centred across the width, with their centres 14 mm from each end. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: A flat plate that mounts a flight-controller stack and attaches to a drone frame, with a central cable pass-through and zip-tie slots for wire management.
intent.part_kind: plate (flight-controller mounting plate for a drone)
stated: Overall plate size: 80 mm long x 60 mm wide x 4 mm thick
All four corners rounded to an 8 mm radius
Four 3.2 mm holes on a 30.5 mm square pattern of centres, centred on the plate, for the flight-controller stack
Four 3.4 mm frame holes on a 64 x 44 mm rectangle of centres, centred on the plate
One 16 mm cable hole in the centre of the plate
Two 16 x 4 mm zip-tie slots running along the plate's length, centred across the width
Zip-tie slot centres are 14 mm from each end
'It carries no load, so there is no load case'
implied: Because it mounts a flight-controller stack via a bolt pattern, the 3.2 mm holes are likely clearance holes for a standard FC mounting standard (e.g. M3-ish), implying fasteners of a size not explicitly stated
Because it bolts to the drone frame via the 3.4 mm hole pattern, the plate needs a reasonably flat, rigid mounting interface so the frame holes line up with the airframe's standoffs
Because it is 3D-printed in PLA, the part's strength and dimensional tolerances will be governed by print orientation and layer adhesion, not treated as isotropic stock
Because zip-tie slots are specified for cable retention, the plate is expected to have wiring routed across or along it that needs to be secured
Because the cable hole is centred, it is implied to pass wiring (e.g. from an ESC or battery) through the plate between two sides/layers of the drone stack
unstated: The fastener/thread size intended for the 3.2 mm and 3.4 mm holes (e.g. M3 clearance), and whether they are clearance or tapped holes
Whether standoffs, spacers, or countersinks are used at the mounting holes, and their dimensions
The depth/thickness tolerance and print layer orientation, which affects whether 4 mm PLA is adequate even for a 'no load' part subjected to handling, vibration, or stack-screw clamping forces
Any vibration, shock, or thermal exposure the plate will see in flight (motors/props nearby), despite the stated absence of a structural load case
The orientation of the zip-tie slots relative to the plate's two faces (through-slot vs. one open side) and their exact placement along the length beyond the 14 mm end offset
Which face of the plate the FC stack mounts on vs. which face faces the frame, i.e. stack-up/orientation
Surface finish, infill percentage, or print settings needed if the part must survive any secondary handling loads
Any requirement for electrical isolation or standoffs between the plate and conductive frame components
Whether the plate needs to clear other components (e.g. battery, camera, antennas) that could constrain hole or slot placement beyond what's given
Tolerance/fit requirements for the 16 mm cable hole and the hole/slot patterns (e.g. positional tolerance for the bolt patterns to mate with a specific aftermarket FC or frame)
risk_signals: Part is for a drone (an unmanned flying vehicle); failure of a mounting plate in flight could contribute to loss of control or a crash, and the brief explicitly disclaims any load case despite the part sitting in a system with vibration, motor torque reaction, and possible impact loads

The brief explicitly states 'it carries no load, so there is no load case,' which is an assertion about the part's duty rather than a given design input, and if untrue (e.g. plate flexes under vibration or stack clamping, or absorbs crash impact) the no-load assumption would be invalidated

assumptions.statement: All specified holes (3.2 mm, 3.4 mm, 16 mm) and slots are plain through-holes/through-slots perpendicular to the plate faces, not tapped, countersunk, or counterbored.
assumptions.rationale: Brief gives only diameters and patterns, with no thread callouts or countersink/counterbore dimensions.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If fasteners require countersinks, counterbores, or threaded holes, the mounting interface may not seat flush or may strip under clamp load.

assumptions.statement: The zip-tie slots pass fully through the plate thickness (open on both faces), not just a recessed channel on one face.
assumptions.rationale: Brief describes them only by length and width, consistent with a conventional through-slot for threading a zip tie.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If slots are meant to be blind/recessed on one face, zip ties could not be routed through as intended.

assumptions.statement: The plate is printed flat (XY plane) with standard PLA settings (e.g. ~20% infill, 2-3 perimeters), typical for a non-structural FDM bracket.
assumptions.rationale: Brief specifies PLA and 3D printing but gives no print orientation, infill, or wall count.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A different orientation or lower infill could change layer-adhesion strength and flatness, affecting fit of the hole patterns.

assumptions.statement: The part operates in typical small-drone ambient conditions (room temperature, no prolonged UV or chemical exposure) consistent with ordinary PLA service limits.
assumptions.rationale: No environmental or thermal exposure stated in the brief; PLA has known limited heat tolerance (~50-60 degC softening).
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If mounted near motors/ESCs generating significant heat, PLA could soften or warp, distorting the hole patterns.

assumptions.statement: The 3.2 mm holes are sized as clearance holes for M3 fasteners (the FC stack's near-universal mounting standard), and the 3.4 mm holes are clearance holes for M3 frame standoffs.
assumptions.rationale: 3.2 mm and 3.4 mm are both common M3 clearance sizes in the drone hobby industry; the brief does not state a thread size explicitly.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a different fastener size is intended, the holes may be too tight or too loose for the actual screws used.

answer.rationale: The plate is a single box, rounded on its own vertical edges (corner_fillet_radius applied via edge_radius/edges:vertical). Zip-tie slots are cut as two profile_slot+extrude cuts chained via subtract directly from the base_plate (each subtract taking the previous result and the new slot extrusion), rather than unioning the slot-cut bodies together, which would restore the material already removed. All hole patterns and the cable hole are then chained as individual tagged hole features cut in sequence from the slotted plate, ending in the terminal cable_hole feature. Hole positions are expressions off the pattern-size parameters so everything stays tied to fc_mount_hole_pattern_size / frame_hole_pattern_width / depth, and slot centers are expressions off ziptie_slot_end_offset and plate_length.
